key_insight: In laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, higher laser power and current strengthen molten-pool convection and penetration, while higher travel speed reduces heat input and narrows the weld.
engineering_relevance: The results help tune hybrid welding parameters to improve weld quality and arc stability when joining low-thermal-expansion Invar components for aerospace tooling.
method: Numerical simulation of molten-pool flow and keyhole behavior
High-speed photography of arc and pool morphology evolution
Parametric study of laser power, welding speed, and current
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent trends across 5-6 kW laser power, 0.5-0.8 m/min speed, and 150-170 A current, linking process changes to penetration depth, weld width, flow intensity, and arc stability.
watch_item: The findings are parameter-window specific, so transferring them to different joint geometries, thicknesses, or equipment may require recalibration.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
